tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). tasks.title: Sparse front boundaries in cell 53,-43 (Kitchener and Sirdar roads): walls, fences, hedges and gates
tasks.notes:
Owner review 2026-11-08 of 53,-43 (southampton-build): very little decor outside house fronts. Not measured yet. Related: #240 (shared frontage between ground and decor), snag S-073. Start by measuring decor per frontage against the aerial and street-run convention, then decide whether the cause is the decor layer or missing boundary evidence. Needs a live world to verify. Spun out of #243 (doors, closed).

DIAGNOSIS 2026-11-09 (read-only; decor report highfield_53_m43_decor-report.json + garden_sources.garden_barriers report).
Measure: 59 eligible fronts in the cell (Kitchener 31, Sirdar 28). 26 have no decor at all. 186 of 1,981 front-yard columns carry decor (~9%), all aerial-hedge fragments. Zero walls, fences or gates; zero furniture in the whole cell (furniture 0). Frontage `boundary` is empty on all 59. Sparse is true on both streets equally.
Aerial (reference/aerial/kitchener-z19 mosaic): fronts are not plain. Most have a low pale wall on the pavement line, side dividing walls or hedges, a paved drive or path gap, gravel/lawn with shrubs, some bins.
Where lost: (1) EVIDENCE, the main cause. A front boundary needs a `front` spec in site/gardens/<street>.json or an aerial hedge (hedge_share >= 0.6). kitchener_road.json has only rear/side vetoes, no `front`; sirdar_road.json does not exist. Aerial hedge fired on 12 of 59 front segments; low walls read pale, not green, so the detector cannot see them. (2) Aerial-hedge fronts never feed residential_frontage `boundary`/`opening` (role_spec only), so those hedges get no entrance gap from the opening logic (route columns are still reserved). (3) No source for private-yard furniture: only map furniture and reference/decor-furniture.json (no 53,-43 entry). (4) NOT the cause: layer drops inside fronts are 29 columns (22 against build, 5 above lidar, 2 blocked); route+clearance take 5-11 columns of 14-58 per yard.
Proposed fix: (a) world data, no code: add `front` (low wall, height 1) and `side_front` to kitchener_road.json and a new sirdar_road.json, citing a registered aerial evidence id; per-house `front: none` where the aerial shows an open drive. (b) code, garden_sources.residential_frontage / garden_barriers: pass the resolved front spec (convention or aerial hedge) into the frontage so `boundary` and `opening` are set for aerial hedges too; widen the opening to the drive width where the route meets a paved strip. Tests in lib/sources/test_garden_sources.py: aerial-hedge front gets an opening; convention front wall leaves the route open. (c) owner decision first: whether to add a front-yard furniture convention (bins beside the opening, planters), labelled inference.
Verify: per-front table before/after (decor columns in extent, boundary length, opening present), decor dry run on 53,-43, then an in-world look along both roads.

OWNER DECISION 2026-11-09: a front yard here should have walls, hedges, fences, bushes, ideally flowers, sheds, garages, ponds and gates. Every element still needs aerial or map evidence per property; nothing is scattered by default. Owning layer for each element: walls, fences, hedges, gates = decor (this task: front/side_front conventions, aerial hedge -> boundary and opening, gate block in the opening; gates are not built today, the opening is left as air). Bushes = trees (bush_voxels for small crowns; check whether front-yard shrubs show in the canopy mask or are lost). Flowers = ground foliage (foliage.py flower list; check whether guessed lawn in private frontage gets any). Sheds and garages = outbuildings: cell_features.py leaves them 'to their house plot' and coverage.py lists OUTBUILDINGS, but nothing appears to build them; this is a gap of its own. Ponds = only mapped natural=water polygons become water_body features; garden ponds from the aerial have no source. Split 2026-11-09 (owner agreed): this task keeps walls, fences, hedges and gates. Sheds and garages moved to #251; bushes, flowers and garden ponds moved to #252. RE-SCOPED 2026-11-10 (docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md): part (a) of the diagnosis, boundary evidence per street, overlaps #255 (district vibe profile); the aerial-hedge opening gap overlaps #240's open item; street furniture is now #260. Blocked by #255. What remains here: the live measurement and the in-world verification against the aerial.

[Review 2026-11-12] Rebuilt 53,-43 ground then decor after #240/#245-247: doors, boundary openings (419 reserved) and routes hold; road-facing fronts still show no boundary (decor = 150 aerial hedge items + 2 mapped iron bars; 79 of 143 frontages ineligible 'no street-run frontage evidence'). Owner confirmed in-world (snag S-077 on I-042). Part (a) of the proposed fix is world data only (front/side_front in kitchener_road.json, new sirdar_road.json, citing a registered aerial evidence id and the owner's Street View for S-073) and needs no code, so it can be done before #255 if the owner wants it sooner; the aerial-hedge opening gap (b) waits on #254. [#252 research 2026-11-12] Planting measured on 53,-43: front gardens have 0 flowers and 0 bushes (59 eligible plots, 1,981 frontage columns), no garden water on the aerial. Bushes and flowers need labelled inference rules, now tasks #265 and #266 (blocked by #253, #254); they add to the rebuild gate. Ponds need no task.

[Research 2026-11-12, docs/plans/244-boundary-evidence-findings.md] Decisions per street run with evidence ids, 7 Kitchener and 13 Sirdar houses read open (front: none), draft data in docs/plans/244-draft/ (kitchener_road.json, sirdar_road.json). tasks.notes:

Keep the door route and frontage opening clear. Verify with per-plot counts before and after and an in-world look. Owner direction 2026-11-10: generic UK-wide. Deliver the three measures above as rules keyed by the #253 class table (gardens first; parks, verges and fields use the same rule table), with no residential-only code paths; park trees stay with the trees layer. Files: lib/layers/trees_layer.py, lib/layers/foliage.py, the ground layer and the #253 table. Check: per-plot before/after counts and a synthetic test for a non-garden class. Ponds may be split into their own follow-up if this grows.

[Design 2026-11-11, docs/plans/land-use-classes.md] Blocked by #254 as well for the code (both edit the ground layer); the three measurements can be taken any time. Rules live in the planting section of config/land-use-classes.json (null means no planting inference) and read the class from parcel meta.land_use, which foliage already reaches through load_area. Tests: plan section 8.

[Research 2026-11-12, measured on 53,-43 with no code or world change; read-only: saved reports, the cached aerial through trees_layer.canopy_grid/cover_grid/find_crowns, garden_sources.frontages_for_cell, live block_scan_summary of the whole cell y28-60] Scope: 143 frontages, 59 eligible (83 'no street-run frontage evidence', 1 no street/number), 1,981 private-frontage columns (Kitchener 31 plots, Sirdar 28). (1) BUSHES: nothing is lost, there is nothing to lose. find_crowns found 101 crowns in the whole cell; only 2 have r<2.0 (bush class) and 1 bush was placed (the other was blocked); front gardens: 0 bushes, 6 trees, 212 canopy-mask columns (11%, trees not shrubs). The mask needs texture+green then a 9-px close and a 0.6 disc mean, and find_crowns drops r<1.5, so garden shrubs of 1-3 columns cannot appear; the looser cover mask sees only 13 front-garden columns (6 not in the canopy mask) across all 59 plots. Driver: aerial shows front gardens as paving or bare lawn, plus the detector floor. Code needed: YES, but as a labelled inference rule (new task 265), not a detector change. (2) FLOWERS: 0 flower blocks and 0 short_grass/tall_grass in the whole cell (live histogram: grass_block 5,410, oak_leaves 10,430, 31 flower_pot decor; no plants). Ground stats: 407 guessed-lawn columns kept as private frontage (+534 aerial-lawn, 523 brick-to-lawn) are the candidate beds. Driver: no pass places flowers; foliage.py REFINE_PLANTS is only a strip/replace allowlist, ground_layer.py only tolerates a plant stem on lawn. Code needed: YES (new task 266). (3) PONDS: none. Strict blue test on the cached aerial (b>r+25, b>=g-5, b>90): 0 water-coloured columns in the cell and 0 inside any frontage extent. No source, no task; revisit only if a place whose aerial shows garden water is built. Not measured: per-plot lawn vs paving split of the 1,981 columns (only the cell-wide 407 guessed-lawn count), shrubs hidden under canopy or roofs, a street-photo check of real gardens (no downloads authorised), the other eligible streets. Decision per street: Kitchener Road and Sirdar Road, same rule (class residential); no street-specific code. Evidence ids: ground report stats highfield_53_m43_ground-report.json, trees report highfield_53_m43_trees-report.json, frontages frontage-kitchener_road-*/frontage-sirdar_road-*. Implementation is split into #265 and #266; #252 stays as the umbrella and the record of these measurements, close it when both land.

tasks.title: District vibe profile: format, loader and boundary and furniture sections
tasks.notes:
Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md section 3. Owner direction 2026-11-10: large areas, few tokens, vibe over 1:1, generic UK-wide. Today only garden_sources.load_convention reads site/gardens/<street>.json (boundaries); decor_plan and ground_layer do not read street conventions, and palette, roof form and storeys are chosen per building by a designer. Deliver: (1) a small JSON profile per district keyed by the #253 land-use class, with the district key decided as a named area listing its cells: site/districts/<slug>.json with name, cells ([tx, tz] entries or inclusive rectangles) and evidence_ids; a cell belongs to at most one district and the loader refuses overlaps (plan section 4) and precedence per-house override, street convention, district profile, class default; (2) a loader in garden_sources beside load_convention that reads a profile as the layer between street convention and class default; (3) this task consumes only the boundary and street-furniture sections (density, and lamp spacing by OSM highway class); palette, roof and storey sections are stored and validated but read by nobody yet (typology trial #257 decides their use); (4) rules/frontage-and-evidence.md section on profiles. Evidence ladder unchanged: a profile is area evidence and never overrides observed data; a missing section means no inference. OSM place polygons are not used (place is not fetched and would tie the key to one map vendor). Blocked by #254 because both change the same frontage code and a profile overrides the class defaults that #254 wires. Files: lib/sources/garden_sources.py, lib/layers/decor_plan.py, lib/layers/ground_layer.py, rules/frontage-and-evidence.md, their tests. Check: unit tests on synthetic profiles (missing section, unknown class, precedence, observed data wins) via python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only <stem>; no world data and no live apply. World work, separate and in the world repo: write the first profile for Kitchener and Sirdar roads (cell 53,-43) from the 2026-11-09 measurement in #244 and the kitchener-z19 aerial, rebuild 53,-43 decor, owner judges street vibe.

[Design 2026-11-11, docs/plans/land-use-classes.md] The loader plugs into land_use.resolve (delivered by #254) as the layer between street convention and class default. Profile sections are keyed by class id and have the same shape as the table's frontage, planting and furniture sections. Tests: plan section 8.

[Added 2026-11-12, review of 53,-43 rebuild] Boundary material fallback. The profile's boundary section must also carry an area-dominant material per boundary kind (e.g. hedge species/block, fence or wall material and height), derived from cited evidence (aerial colour, street photos), not guessed. Ladder for material as well as presence: per-house override with its own evidence (exact material, e.g. a 2 m light fence at one house becomes beech planks) > street convention > district profile dominant material (e.g. mostly dark hedges: spruce-leaf hedge when in doubt) > class default. Labelled inference, never `observed`, and it never overrides observed data. Test: a district dominated by dark hedges gives spruce hedge for an unevidenced front, while a per-house light-fence override keeps its own material.

[Research 2026-11-12, docs/plans/244-boundary-evidence-findings.md] Material evidence: Kitchener Road is dominated by about 1 m weathered timber fence (Street View 67 Kitchener Rd) with brick wall at 68, 66, 64, 62, 48, 46 and hedge at 41, 43, 54, 63; Sirdar Road is hedge where a boundary shows (no street view, aerial inference) and 46% open. The dominant material varies by street run here, so the profile should key the dominant material by street run (or frontage block) with per-house overrides. Draft convention files in docs/plans/244-draft/ express this and are the test fixtures to mirror.

[Owner decision 2026-11-12, #244 review] Close-boarded fence panels are plank blocks, default oak_planks, with tone variants (dark spruce/dark_oak, reddy jungle/acacia/mangrove, pale birch) chosen per run from evidence; slatted runs use the normal fence block. The profile's material vocabulary needs a plank tone table (docs/plans/244-boundary-evidence-findings.md) and the rules section for profiles should carry it. Verify first whether decor_plan/decor_layer place and join a plank barrier (barrier kinds and JOINABLE name only brick_wall, iron_bars, spruce_fence).

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Provider-neutral lidar: ghost, query, extremes and readiness resolve by type; a world's own lidar row beats the system row; documented provider contract
tasks.notes: Owner direction 2026-11-10: other people using the toolkit install their own providers; tool code asks for a reference type, never a vendor (#28 covered only the lidar world and tiles modules). Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md. Evidence (checked in code): (1) shims/lidar_ghost.py, lidar_query.py and lidar_extremes.py call load_provider('ukdefra-lidar', ...) with a literal id; callers are lib/layers/ground_layer.py:119, lib/journal/cell_preparation.py:57, scripts/cell_registry.py:132 and 149, scripts/cell_marker.py:470 and 494. (2) load_place_sources (lib/sources/cell_sources.py ~99-110) lists system rows before world rows and lidar_provider_row returns the first lidar match, so a locally installed lidar row never beats the system one, for world and tiles too. (3) lib/journal/readiness_evidence.py lidar_status (~63-85) uses pick_uri, TILE_MB, tiles_for and client.cache/catalogue/<E>E-<N>N.json and client.tiles, a provider-specific interface that cell preparation depends on. (4) lib/sources/test_lidar_provider.py mocks load_lidar_module, so it checks row choice only. (5) ghost planning catches LookupError as 'no lidar for cell', so a no-provider LookupError would be swallowed. Reviewer-checked: lidar_ghost is vendor-neutral apart from a 4-line default_heights, and ghost_owners_for needs no lidar; lidar_query and lidar_extremes hard-import defra_lidar, DEFRA_CRS and --bbox-osgb; no core code imports them, but .agents/skills/new-world-build/SKILL.md:90 names lidar_extremes. Unverified: whether a provider outside England can meet the readiness tile interface as it stands. Deliver: (a) world-over-system precedence for the lidar catalogue row, with a test; (b) lidar_ghost as shared code that samples through lidar_provider (not a catalogue role), with default_heights moved into the provider; (c) query and extremes as catalogue modules roles resolved by type, copying the shims/lidar_world.py pattern; (d) readiness_evidence.lidar_status reads missing tiles and tile identity through a provider-neutral method on the tile client; (e) a typed no-provider error instead of LookupError; (f) extend the lidar contract already in reference/TYPES.txt (and fix its stale scripts/ path) with entry points, model names DTM and DSM, missing(), sample(), the mc_heights keys, crs and the tile and cost methods, and update the seams table in docs/provider-name-audit.md. Out of scope: writing a real second provider; a fallback height source where no lidar exists. Files: shims/lidar_ghost.py, lidar_query.py, lidar_extremes.py, _provider_shim.py; lib/sources/lidar_provider.py, cell_sources.py, config/system-providers.json; lib/layers/ground_layer.py; lib/journal/cell_preparation.py, readiness_evidence.py; scripts/cell_registry.py, cell_marker.py; reference/TYPES.txt; docs/provider-name-audit.md; tests. Check: a new test with a synthetic second lidar provider in a temp world, with the system row still present, run in a fresh process (scripts/run_tests.py is one process and the shims overwrite sys.modules): the shims, the registry and readiness pick it up; a static assertion that no catalogue id appears in shims/lidar_*.py; python3 scripts/check_provider_names.py still passes. Trials #256-#259 outside the first world's country depend on this being done or on the trial naming its own height source.

tasks.title: Reduce decor surface probing cost with bounded bulk scans
tasks.notes: Measured by #229: rules/slow-commands.md, Decor stage measurements (2026-11-11). On one already-built live benchmark cell (southampton-build 53,-43), two unchanged decor applies planned 2583 positions/630 boxes with zero mismatches. Planning took 184.027/180.585 s; in run 2 live surface snapshot alone took 140.235 s (n=1 for nested stage). Investigate grouping nearby column scans under MCP volume and LiveBlocks memory limits; collect scan counts and parsing time before choosing grouping. A 25–50% stage reduction would save 35–70 s/apply, an untested scenario rather than a promised saving. Preserve fresh live observations, unknown/unloaded states, cell clipping, masks, ownership, and identical placements/undo. No evidence downloads, world rebuild or new planning engine. Extend existing synthetic decor snapshot/scan tests to show fewer transport calls without cache thrashing, including long fences and outbuildings. Run python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_decor_layer --only test_block_store; benchmark live only when separately authorised. World timing logs/results: verification/timing-task-229-2026-11-11/ in the named world.

tasks.title: Reuse validated source preparation between redo preview and live planning
tasks.notes: Follow-up justified by #229, rules/slow-commands.md (2026-11-11). Decor redo preview took 50.471 s, including 0.974 s disk surface probing. Apply planning outside live surface probing took 40.350 s. Exact duplicated work is not measured. Investigate a narrow shared seam for immutable source-derived plot/evidence preparation across the existing preview/apply flow under its one lock. Profile first; retain preview and fresh live block reads, verify source and journal identities, fail closed on intervening changes, preserve readiness and all journal/mask/ownership/undo checks. Do not cache or reuse stale live geometry, remove validation, or add a new geometry engine. Estimated 20–40 s/redo saving assumes part of the overlapping source work is reusable; validate that assumption before implementation and record if no safe saving is worthwhile. Synthetic tests for reuse and invalidation on source/journal change, unchanged plans and zero bypass of live readback; no world data in tests or live apply in this ticket without separate authorisation.

tasks.title: Labelled shrub inference on guessed private lawn, keyed by land-use class
tasks.notes: From #252 research (2026-11-12): front gardens in 53,-43 have 0 bushes; the aerial gives no shrub signal (2 bush-size crowns in the cell, 13 cover columns across 59 plots), so shrubs can only be a labelled inference. Add a planting.shrubs rule to config/land-use-classes.json (null = none; residential ships a low density per metre of front boundary or house wall, e.g. one bush per 6 guessed-lawn columns along the building line; the value is a starting guess for the owner to tune) read via the parcel's meta.land_use. Place plant_cell_canopy.bush_voxels only on guessed lawn (soft_grass, never observed or mapped surface), outside reserved door route, openings and footprints, with may_plant air checks; provenance source inference, low confidence. Prefer extending trees_layer.py or the decor pass over a new pass; no residential-only branch. Files: lib/layers/trees_layer.py (or decor), config/land-use-classes.json, lib/sources/land_use.py. Tests (synthetic): a residential class row places bushes only on guessed lawn; a null-planting class (park, rural) places none; route and opening columns stay clear; deterministic for a seed; observed lawn untouched. Check: per-plot bush counts before/after on 53,-43 in a preview, no apply. Detector change is NOT wanted.

tasks.title: Flower beds on guessed private lawn, keyed by land-use class
tasks.notes: From #252 research (2026-11-12): 0 flower blocks and 0 grass plants in the whole of 53,-43 (live scan); 407 guessed-lawn columns kept as private frontage are the candidates. Add a planting.flowers rule to config/land-use-classes.json (null = none; residential: sparse beds, a small fraction of guessed-lawn columns, clustered against the house wall or boundary, one or two flower kinds per plot from foliage.REFINE_PLANTS). Place in the ground pass as a plant block at gy+1 on grass_block only (ground_layer already tolerates a stem on lawn, STEM_OR_FLOWER), on guessed lawn only, never on the door route, opening, observed lawn or under a tree/decor mask. Labelled inference, provenance low confidence. Files: lib/layers/ground_layer.py, lib/layers/foliage.py, config/land-use-classes.json. Tests (synthetic): flowers appear only on guessed lawn of a class with a flowers rule; none for null-planting classes, observed lawn, route or opening columns; re-running the plan is idempotent and a redo strips them (is_refine_foliage). Check: per-plot flower counts before/after in a preview on 53,-43, no apply.

tasks.title: Thin closers for diagonal fence panel runs instead of solid plank cubes
tasks.notes: From the 53,-43 checkpoint 2026-11-13 after #273: runs are continuous and face one way, but the closers at diagonal steps are solid oak plank cubes that look chunky beside the thin shelves (largest one in the foreground of the west view from 6808,38,-5418). Owner: fix the closers. Deliver: thin closers. Preferred: a shelf in the step column turned onto the perpendicular axis (east or west facing for a north/south run, and the reverse) so its 3/16 back board continues the line of the neighbouring boards on the inner (owned) side, with the open front on the outward side; if geometry shows a perpendicular shelf cannot close the corner without a visible gap, use the thin fence block of the same wood for that one column and say so. State the choice and why from the shelf geometry (back board 3/16 flush with the edge opposite the facing, 2/16 lips top and bottom; see docs/plans/244-boundary-evidence-findings.md 'Shelf panels'). Closers must never land on road or owned-by-other columns, and entrance openings (#270) must stay open. Also re-check the few stretches where the planned run still mixes facings (near x 6799-6803, z -5418..-5416 on 53,-43) and fix them if the cause is the same run grouping. Tests: synthetic 27 and 45 degree runs and an axis-aligned run: no solid cube remains in a panel run unless the run has no outward evidence, every consecutive pair of columns is joined by a board edge (corner-touching still counts as a gap), facing constant per run. Check, read-only: the character map script (/private/tmp/claude-507/-Users-cjg-Projects-ai-worldbuilder/0e5bd3f8-1754-41d4-8289-b3fceedd6fc6/scratchpad/shelfmap.py) before and after, with a legend for the closer symbol. No apply, no rebuild; the owner reviews in-world afterwards.
